scope.note: The bundled binaries are byte-exact for Black 2/White 2 and the supported VW2R build. The PDF discusses Black/White behavior too, but this profile does not claim that B2W2 bytecode is an exact Black/White script source.

documentation.title: Enemy AI in Gen V Pokémon

scriptPackage.linkContext: Direct script-files hyperlink in the documentation PDF.

semanticNormalization.authority: Authored structured projection of the hash-pinned PDF; independently checked by verify_trainer_ai_semantics.py.

authorityPolicy.binaryScriptEvidence: Authoritative for observed opcode identity, argument word count, and use sites.
authorityPolicy.externalParserEvidence: Corroborating syntax evidence only. Conflicts remain explicit and never override exact binary alignment.
authorityPolicy.engineSymbolEvidence: Corroborating function identity and location evidence only. A symbol name or address is not executable behavior.
authorityPolicy.executableSemantics: Requires handler implementation analysis plus independent validation before prediction can consume it.

engineBindings.authority: Exact clean White 2 and VW2R overlay identity plus dispatcher-to-SWAN binding; handler names remain identity evidence, not behavior.

engineSemantics.authority: Exact clean White 2/VW2R handler and VM byte ranges, dispatcher identities, call sequences, and material constants; only listed commands are promoted.

actionSemantics.authority: Exact clean White 2/VW2R overlay 167 action-region and reachable item-record verification.

itemBattleParameters.authority: Exact decoded clean White 2 and VW2R item-record hold-effect and Fling-power fields, independently checked against both pinned ROMs.

moveSelection.multiBattleScoring: Each usable move is scored separately against each legal target.
moveSelection.rotationScoring: Target is selected randomly, then Singles-style move scoring is applied.

trainerDataBindings.note: Game datasets bind numeric trainer item IDs to their own items.json and expose decoded flag IDs from the mask. Existing low-byte ai fields may remain as compatibility fields.

researchCoverage.evidenceBoundary: Exact dispatcher bindings establish identity only. The separately verified engine-semantics batch promotes only its listed handlers; every other undocumented handler remains fail-closed.

condition.note: Use the exact token vocabulary in the PDF; preserved source tokens include apparent documentation spellings such as cond.embaro.

documentationScope.note: Structured from the supplied prose. It does not fill command opcodes absent from the PDF glossary.

eligibility: active Pokémon is not under Embargo
trainer has an unused item in one of four ordered bag slots
itemSelection.dataDependency: The game dataset must map each trainer bag item to the applicable itemClass and cured status or raised stat; prose alone is not an item-ID table.

prerequisites: at least one legal reserve is not already selected to switch in

triggers.condition: target has Wonder Guard; user lacks a super-effective move; a reserve has one
at least two damaging moves and none can hit by type effectiveness
Choice Band, Specs, or Scarf has locked the user

triggers.precheck: If user has a super-effective move, skip this trigger with probability 2/3.
notes: Overgrow is the documented engine bug; Mold Breaker-family bypass and Levitate are not considered.

triggers.condition: Natural Cure is active, HP is at least 50%, and status is Sleep or Freeze
notes: Resistance is type-only; no damage simulation or ability is considered.

prechecks: If user has a super-effective move, skip with probability 9/10.
Skip when total signed stat-stage changes are at least -38.
Skip when user took no damage on the previous turn.
candidateRequirements: reserve has a super-effective move against selected target
notes: The -38 comparison is documented as a likely engine bug rather than corrected to the likely intended +4.

invocation: switch-out trigger that did not select a specific reserve

candidateScore.result: highest adjusted move power per reserve

notes: Only the leading group tied for the optimum is guaranteed to retain party order; simultaneous later replacements can reorder tied runner-up candidates.

moveSelection.bypass: A forced continuation of a multi-turn move bypasses ordinary selection.

battleStyles.single: Score every usable move against the opposing target.
battleStyles.doubleOrTriple: Score each usable move independently against every legal target, then uniformly resolve highest-score move-target ties.
battleStyles.rotation: Uniformly select a player field target, then use Singles scoring with the randomly selected attacker.

randomSources.freshCommandRandom: Every JumpIfRand command draws a new uniform byte.
randomSources.commonRandom: One uniform byte is drawn for each Pokémon at the start of its move-selection process and reused by all JumpIfRandSeed comparisons during that process.

validationCases.expected: Potion is selected; stored order is preserved and scanning stops at the first usable item.

validationCases.input: A healing item is usable but Embargo is active.
Final Perish Song turn with a legal reserve.
Two ordered reserves both match the relevant immunity ability.
validationCases.expected: First candidate probability is 1/2, second is 1/4, and no switch through this trigger is 1/4.

validationCases.input: A damaging move has encoded base power below 10.
validationCases.expected: Its switch-in comparison power is 60 before type scaling.
Left, right, and remain are each 1/3.

validationCases.input: Three legal move-target options share the highest final score.
validationCases.expected: Each option is selected with probability 1/3.

validationCases.input: Several JumpIfRandSeed comparisons occur during one Pokémon selection pass.
validationCases.expected: All comparisons use the same initially sampled byte; probabilities must not be multiplied as independent draws.

validationCases.input: Equivalent comparisons use opcode 0x15 and opcode 0x24.
A revealed opponent ability remains stored while another Pokémon switches into that field slot.
validationCases.expected: GetAbilityGuess returns the slot-stored ability until replaced or the slot Pokémon faints.

exactScope.rule: Exact when the evaluation request supplies every state/query dependency reached by these programs; missing request state remains path-local fail-closed.

blockers.detail: These commands are confined to non-VW2R active flags or the preserved flag12 source-layout conflict and do not block the verified VW2R trainer flag closure.

predictionReadiness.consumerRule: Execute the verified VW2R flag/item closure. Fail only a reached unsupported flag, command, item identity, or missing request field; never redistribute unresolved mass.

provenance.authorityPolicy: Exact B2W2/VW2R binary and handler evidence controls engine semantics. Hash-pinned PDF semantics may fill only its explicit documented scope. Names, symbols, secondary prose, and analogies never promote unresolved commands.

randomSources.correlation: one common byte reused by opcodes 0x6F/0x70 throughout the pass

fresh except manual switch reuses switch-target

fresh at each documented tie stage

limitations.note: Commands after 0x2A are preserved with exact binary opcode, plaintext token, parameters, and use sites. Only commands listed in the independently verified engine-semantics batch are executable; all others remain unresolved.
The supplied PDF gives JumpIfHasAnyStatus a positive heading but duplicates JumpIfHasNoStatus prose. Exact handler analysis proves the nonzero-status branch, so the heading is authoritative.

The supplied source presentation assigns one 32-bit word to each command, but the exact AINop62/AINop63 handlers consume zero operands under the verified VM model. Preserve the bytes and keep flag12 non-executable until the stream is independently re-decoded.

The pinned public sources and exact overlay 170 dispatcher bind all 120 opcodes to handlers, but handler identity is not behavior. Implementation analysis and independent known-answer validation remain required before prediction can consume unresolved opcodes.
Do not use these B2W2 binaries as byte-exact Black/White scripts without a separately pinned and verified Black/White profile.
